[engine] An edit tool's success message is not evidence the edit is in the tree, and edits issued in PARALLEL against one file silently lose writes. After every batch of edits to a single file, verify with `git diff -U0 -- <file> | grep '^@@'` plus a targeted grep for the removed strings; never stack a build on top of an unverified edit.

**class**: `source-reading`

## 為什麼（because）

Three Edit calls were issued in a single message against llama-context.cpp (remove cgc_s1_tag() from the L4 identity map, remove it from the gather identity map, and drop the two guard terms that tested it). All three returned 'Successfully edited file'. Grepping the file afterwards found the first two strings still present at lines 5145 and 5966 while the third was gone -- one landed, two were silently dropped, and the reports were identical. Compounding it, the same run had removed the DEFINITIONS of cgc_s1_tag()/cgc_s1_ident() earlier, so the file was left referring to functions that no longer existed: a state that cannot compile, and that no success message would have revealed. This is the second occurrence of the class in one session -- an earlier attempt to add the ffn_moe_down capture and rewrite the fast-path call site also reported success without writing bytes, caught only because the string `CGC-S1: OUT` was found inside the built dylib while never appearing in any log. The distinctive signature is a probe that is compiled in and provably never fires.

## 反例（counterexample_observed）

Three 'Successfully edited' returns on one file: one landed, two absent from disk, and the file left calling deleted functions.

## 適用於（applies_to）

- `src/llama.cpp/src/llama-context.cpp`
- `src/llama.cpp/src/llama-expert-cache.cpp`
- `agent_harness/CONVENTIONS.md`
